Records.Body:
Part of #2388 (harness-native program #2387). The **net-new** half of #2403.

## Thesis
The native owned-loop stream (`runNativeArmStream`, `internal/gateway/native_serve.go`)
hand-builds **text-only** Anthropic SSE. Everything the owned loop does between
`message_start` and `message_stop` — turn boundaries, per-call adjudication verdicts,
tool dispatch, result admission/taint — is invisible until the terminal `ArmMetrics`
witness on `message_stop`. An operator or client cannot watch *what the loop is doing*
mid-flight; it can only read the prose and the final counters.

The interrupt/command half of #2403 is already substantially built (the session control
plane — `POST /v1/fak/session/{id}/{verb}` run/budget/pace/priority/wall/throughput
verbs, plus the steer route with `class:"now"` boundary-interrupt semantics and the
`#2758` terminate signal). What is genuinely missing is the **outbound** half: the stream
carrying the loop's *typed state*, not just its prose. This issue ships that spine.

## Distilled inspiration (never copied)
The reference harness's stream carries provenance-tagged loop-state events (each tied to
its originating call), not only text. fak's version additionally carries **kernel
verdicts** — the adjudication reason classes a client can gate on — drawn from the same
closed vocabulary the rest of the kernel refuses with. Every emitted event is a witnessed
fact about a real lifecycle transition, never narration.

## Design
1. **`internal/agent`** — a typed, nil-safe loop-progress observer (a pure additive
   `RunOption`, in the family of `WithSessionGate` / `WithSpeculator`):
   - `ProgressEvent{Kind, Turn, CallID, Tool, Verdict, Reason, Taint}` with a
     `ProgressEventKind` closed set: `turn_started`, `call_adjudicated`, `tool_started`,
     `result_admitted`, `turn_done`.
   - `WithProgressObserver(func(ProgressEvent)) RunOption` sets `runConfig.observer`.
   - `runArm` calls a nil-safe `cfg.emitProgress(...)` at each lifecycle point. When no
     observer is wired the emit is a no-op, so the historical loop stays **byte-for-byte
     unchanged** (the same guarantee every other `RunOption` carries).
2. **`internal/gateway`** — `runNativeArmStream` wires `WithProgressObserver` to emit a
   typed **custom SSE event** per `ProgressEvent` (`send(kind, payload)`), interleaved
   with the existing text deltas, each tagged with the session trace and originating
   call id. The observer runs on the same request goroutine as the text sink (the loop is
   synchronous within `CompleteStream`), so no cross-goroutine send race is introduced.

## Acceptance (witnessable, on-box)
Golden SSE test `TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents` in `internal/gateway`: a multi-turn
`serve --native` stream in which one tool call is **denied** and one is **executed**
emits the full typed event sequence **in order** — `turn_started` →
(`tool_started` → `call_adjudicated{verdict}` → `result_admitted{taint}`)+ → `turn_done`
per turn — interleaved with the text deltas, terminating on `message_stop` carrying the
`fak.native_arm` `ArmMetrics`. Runs under a deterministic mock streaming planner (no model
serving), witnessed via WSL `go test` against the committed tip.

## Out of scope (tracked follow-on)
- The **inbound** command half of #2403 (`TestInterruptLandsAtTurnBoundary`) — the session
  control plane already carries the mechanism; a boundary-lands witness test is a sibling
  follow-on, filed separately.

## Seams
- `internal/agent/loop.go` (runArm lifecycle points), `internal/agent/loop_session.go`
  (`runConfig`, `RunOption`)
- `internal/gateway/native_serve.go` (`runNativeArmStream` SSE synthesis)

## Parent context
Part of #2388 (harness-native program #2387).

## Current state
`runNativeArmStream` emits text-only SSE; loop lifecycle state is invisible until the
terminal ArmMetrics on `message_stop`.

## Why now
This is the outbound half of loop ownership — streaming that carries the loop's state, the
precondition for any client that watches, gates on, or reacts to a running native loop.

## Expected steps
1. Add the typed observer + `WithProgressObserver` `RunOption` in `internal/agent`.
2. Emit at the runArm lifecycle points, nil-safe.
3. Wire the observer to typed SSE events in `runNativeArmStream`.
4. Add and green the golden test `TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents`.

## Batch policy
Single coherent slice, landed once — no spam of per-event commits.

## Done when
`TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents` is green on the committed tip and the native stream
emits the typed event sequence with the historical (unwired) loop byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/3 points.

production

Records.Body:
Parent: #3006. Follow-on from #3020 (the MTP/speculative-decoding evaluation gate).

## Why now
#3020 landed the evaluation gate: the deepseekbench scorecard now carries a `speculative = off | mtp | dspark` axis and an `accepted_token_ratio` field, and `CompareSpeedup` refuses to credit a speculative speedup without verified quality parity. That gate is the precondition this native ticket must pass before it can claim a win. No native draft head lands until an external-engine mtp-vs-off run produces a real target.

## Engine metric (named, per #3020 done-condition c)
Accepted-token ratio == mean accepted draft length per verify pass.
- In-kernel closure: `internal/polymodel/specdecode.go` `SpecDecodeRun.MeanAcceptanceLength`.
- Scorecard field: `accepted_token_ratio` on the deepseekbench `Row` (added by #3020).

## Target acceptance threshold (named, per #3020 done-condition c)
Mean acceptance length >= X at `quality_parity = verified`, where X is taken from the measured external mtp-vs-off scorecard rows. Interim floor 1.5 (drafting must buy >= 50% extra accepted tokens per verify pass) — replace with the measured X once an engine that exposes the acceptance counter is chosen.

## In scope
- Native DeepSeek-V4 MTP (NextN depth-1) draft head on the pure-fak decode path.
- Wire draft-accept through `internal/modelroute/specbridge.go` (`SpecAccept`/`AcceptFunc`).
- Emit `accepted_token_ratio` into the deepseekbench row from the live acceptance counter.

## Out of scope
- Any speedup claim not paired with verified quality parity (the #3020 gate refuses it).
- DSpark-specific engine internals (separate lever).

## Substrate already shipped
- `polymodel.SpecDecode` live loop (#4877, closed).
- Loader NextN/MTP skip: `internal/ggufload` `num_nextn_predict_layers` parse.
- Eval plan: docs/notes/DEEPSEEK-V4-MTP-SPECULATIVE-EVAL-2026-07-08.md.
Related: #23 (generic native verify-accept), #3197 (EAGLE-3).

## Done condition
- [ ] Native V4 MTP depth-1 draft head produces drafts on the pure-fak decode path.
- [ ] Live acceptance counter feeds `accepted_token_ratio`; a speedup row only prints when mean acceptance length >= the named threshold AND quality_parity=verified.
- [ ] One issue-bound commit with a fail-before/pass-after test and DOS witness.

Records.Title: feat(loop): structured mid-flight session verbs — interrupt / drop-pending-call / set-budget at the turn boundary (#2388)
Records.Body:
## Summary

Split from the write-half of #2403 (parent epic #2388). The **read half** —
typed loop-progress SSE (`turn_started` → `tool_started` → `call_adjudicated` →
`result_admitted` → `turn_done`) emitted by the owned loop and projected into
structured native SSE — is delivered by **#5148**. This ticket tracks the
**write half**: structured *mid-flight* session verbs that let an operator steer
a running `serve --native` loop, landing their effect at the next **clean turn
boundary** with a tamper-evident journal witness.

Now that the loop's state is legible (the read half), an operator can finally
act on it. Today the native loop is drive-able only at the request boundary
(run-state / budget / pace via the session table); there is no way to reach into
a turn that is already in flight.

## Scope

Three structured verbs, each landing at the next turn boundary (never mid-tool,
never mid-adjudication):

- **`interrupt`** — stop the loop at the next boundary with a closed-token
  witness, distinct from a hard cancel/terminate. Reuses the existing
  terminate seam + `ArmMetrics.StoppedBySession`.
- **`drop-pending-call`** — skip a specific queued tool call by `call_id` before
  it is dispatched. This is the **net-new** piece: the loop has no per-call skip
  consult today. *(design risk — flagged below.)*
- **`set-budget`** — adjust the live token/turn budget the loop reads each turn
  (the session table already carries budget; this is the mid-flight setter).

## Acceptance

`TestInterruptLandsAtTurnBoundary` (and per-verb siblings): an `interrupt`
issued while turn *N* is dispatching tool calls does **not** cut a tool or an
adjudication short — the loop completes turn *N*'s admitted results, then stops
at the boundary carrying the closed witness token; the journal records the verb,
its arrival, and the boundary it landed at. `drop-pending-call` skips exactly the
named `call_id` and nothing else. Byte-for-byte invariant: with no verb issued,
the loop is the historical loop (the same guard the read half honors).

## Reuse targets (verified against the tree)

- **Boundary-drain seam** already lands operator input at the clean turn boundary:
  `internal/agent/loop.go` (after `cfg.gateTurn`, ~L463–505). `interrupt` reuses
  the terminate seam + the `ArmMetrics.StoppedBySession` closed token.
- **Closed op/witness vocabulary already declared** in
  `internal/sessionctl/vocab.go`: `OpPause/OpResume/OpCancel/OpTerminate/OpBudget`,
  `OpSpec`, and `WitnessBoundaryStop`/`WitnessSafePointStop`. A new interrupt verb
  registers an `OpSpec{Witness: WitnessBoundaryStop}` — no new vocabulary invented.
- **Durable write-through** for a persisted verb: `applySessionControlDurable` →
  `mirror.writeThrough` (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go`).
- **Observer seam (read half, #5148)** gives the write half its acceptance
  witness: an `interrupt` should surface as a `turn_done`-then-stop in the same
  structured SSE stream, so the operator sees their verb take effect.

## Design risk

`drop-pending-call` is the only piece with no existing seam: the loop must
consult a per-`call_id` skip set *before* dispatching each queued `tc` in the
tool-call loop. Needs a small, nil-safe skip-consult (same additive-RunOption
shape as `WithProgressObserver`) so the historical loop is unchanged when unused.

---

Records.Title: feat(bench): coalescebench — net-tok/s(B) curve + coalescing ratio for SSD-offloaded MoE
Records.Body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §2. Depends on: A (`SimulateExpertCacheBatch`).

## What

A deterministic replay bench (new `cmd/coalescebench`, mirroring `cmd/batchbench`) that drives
the cross-agent coalescing simulator over synthetic (and later real, #H) GLM-5.2-shaped routing
traces at **B = 1, 4, 16, 64, 128** and emits the **net-tok/s(B) curve** plus the coalescing
ratio `C(B) = (B·K)/U(B)`, applying the §2 roofline:

```
t_agent(B) = max( SSD_term(B), RAM_term, FLOP_term )
net_toks(B) = B / t_agent(B)
SSD_term(B) = (DistinctStreamed_per_step · expert_bytes) / (B · BW_ssd)
```

Bench inputs (`BW_ssd`, `BW_ram`, `expert_bytes`, `NR`, K, N, L) are **flags with GLM-5.2
header-derived defaults** cited to `GLM52-DGX-THEORETICAL-CEILING`; every emitted row is labelled
**PROJECTED** (roofline, not a served measurement) except a future `--trace` mode fed by #H.

## Why

Turns the epic's projected coalescing curve into a **witnessed, deterministic, zero-hardware**
number — the table the demo (#I), the metric (#C), and the honest headline all rest on. Reports
the two baselines from §2.1 side by side so the 4–10×+ is never stated without its denominator:
`× vs B un-coalesced streams` (the defensible headline) and `× vs single-agent latency` (labelled
aggregate/latency-tolerant only).

## DoD

- [ ] `cmd/coalescebench` prints a markdown table: `B | U(B) | C(B) | SSD_term | net_toks | ×vs-uncoalesced | ×vs-1agent | binding-roofline`.
- [ ] A synthetic router with a tunable skew knob (uniform → Zipf) so `U(B)` growth is inspectable; default skew cites a source or is labelled a placeholder.
- [ ] The regime transition (B* where `SSD_term` drops below `RAM_term` → the box goes effectively resident) is detected and printed.
- [ ] Determinism test in `cmd/coalescebench` (or `internal/`): same seed/flags → identical table (no `Math.random`/time).
- [ ] A `docs/benchmarks/` results note with the projected curve, every cell labelled, and the explicit statement that it is a roofline pending #H's real-trace witness.
- [ ] New leaf `coalescebench` gets its architest tier row (`TestEveryPackageDeclaresTier`) and, if import-free at root, `pureRoot`.

## Files

`cmd/coalescebench/` (new), `docs/benchmarks/COALESCE-NET-TOKS-RESULTS.md` (new), architest tier
row. CPU-only, **no hardware gate**.

Records.Title: fix(fleet): add age-based retention to the worktree-doctor sweep archive (4.6GB leak) (fak fleet)
Records.Body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 1 of that census — the LARGEST leak by bytes, and a pointed
irony: the collector for one leak (stray worktrees) is itself the creator of this
one. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`tools/worktree_doctor.py` `do_sweep` (around lines 580-596) archives every dirty
swept worktree to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/watchdog/worktree-archive/<date>/` (via
`archive_worktree` / `_default_archive_dir`, around lines 609-615) BEFORE force-
removing it. There is no reaper — nothing anywhere in the repo ever deletes an
archive day. Evidence: `worktree-archive/2026-07-14` alone holds 16 full worktree
copies = 4.6GB (one is 1.3GB — full build artifacts archived wholesale). This is
the single largest create-without-collect leak by bytes on the live tree.

## Fix direction

Add age-based retention to the archive directory: after a sweep writes a new
archive day (or at the start of `do_sweep`), prune archive-day directories older
than a bounded window. Pick a conservative default (e.g. 7 days — long enough to
recover a mistakenly-swept worktree, short enough to bound 4.6GB/2-week growth);
make it a named constant / overridable via the same config channel the doctor
already uses for its other knobs.

Safety: an archive day is a post-mortem copy of an ALREADY-swept (dirty) worktree
— it is a recovery convenience, not live state. Deleting an OLD archive day past
the window is safe; deleting a RECENT one is not (someone may still want to
recover a same-week accidental sweep). So age, with a generous floor, is the
correct signal here (unlike the wip-ref case where recoverability, not age,
decides). Never delete the archive day created by the current sweep run.

## Likely files

- tools/worktree_doctor.py (add archive-day retention in/around `do_sweep` / `archive_worktree`)

## Expected steps

1. Read `do_sweep`, `archive_worktree`, `_default_archive_dir` and confirm the
   `worktree-archive/<date>/` layout and how the date-day directories are named.
2. Add an age-based prune of archive-day directories older than the window
   (default 7 days), guarded so the current run's archive day is never removed.
3. Add a test: seed several `worktree-archive/<date>/` day dirs with dummy
   content, some older than the window and some fresh, run the prune, assert only
   the stale days are removed and fresh ones (incl. today's) survive. Mirror the
   existing tools test style.
4. Re-measure the live archive tree after a doctor run and confirm total archive
   bytes stop climbing past the window.

## Batch policy

One retention prune for one leak. Do not fan out per-archive-day or per-worktree
tickets; the prune sweeps all stale days in one pass. Do not touch other census
rows in this change.

## Work estimate

2 points. An age-based directory prune plus a temp-dir retention test, in an
isolated Python tool file with no cross-package coupling.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Closes the
largest-by-bytes row of the 12-site survey (4.6GB reclaimable).

## Target operating envelope

- retention tests: >= 1 case
- stale archive days pruned while fresh ones and today survive: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- retention tests: >= 1 case
- stale archive days pruned while fresh ones and today survive: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

Records.Title: feat(accounts): fak guard finds no Claude login on macOS — read Claude Code's Keychain credentials
Records.Body:
On a Mac where the operator is logged into Claude Code (2.x), `fak guard` refuses to launch:

    fak guard: no Claude subscription token found and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, and stdin is not a terminal — refusing to spawn a headless agent ... login=needs_login can_serve=false

Root cause: every fak credential probe is disk-only — `hasClaudeCredentials` / `resolveAnthropicOAuthToken` / `readLiveAccessToken` / `credExpiresAt` / `credExpiry` read `<config>/.credentials.json` and `<config>/.oauth-token`. Claude Code on macOS stores the live subscription OAuth credential in the login Keychain instead (generic password, service `Claude Code-credentials`, account `$USER`; a non-default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` login appends `-<first 8 hex of sha256(NFC(dir))>` to the service). The plaintext file is only Claude Code's fallback store, so on a healthy Mac none of the probed files exist and every seat reads as `needs_login`.

Fix: one Keychain reader in `internal/accounts` (exec `/usr/bin/security find-generic-password -a <user> -w -s <service>`, darwin-only seam, short TTL cache, credential-safe), consulted as a fallback by:
- `hasClaudeCredentials` (login posture / `guardSubscriptionLoginPresent`)
- the guard OAuth token loader (between `.credentials.json` and `.oauth-token`)
- `credExpiresAt` / `credExpiry` (headless StaleCred rung, park-for-relogin, TriggerRefresh)
- `readLiveAccessToken` (account failover picker)

Non-darwin behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (the seam is nil). Verified end to end on a Mac with a live Keychain login: `fak guard status` reports ready/can_serve and a guarded session boots.

Records.Title: fix(dos): dos_commit_audit silently ignores its commit argument and audits HEAD, so a witness verdict can be attributed to the wrong sha
Records.Body:
## What happens

The `dos` MCP tool `dos_commit_audit` accepts a `commit` argument and **silently ignores it**, auditing `HEAD` instead. It reports the HEAD sha in its own `sha` field, so the response looks well-formed and authoritative — it is simply about a different commit than the one asked about.

Three calls, three different `commit` values, one workspace (`C:\work\fak`):

| `commit` passed | `sha` returned | `source_files` returned |
|---|---|---|
| `bc0988c11` | `b66a2dba5` | `internal/agent/stream_stall.go`, … |
| `affbb1c70` | `b66a2dba5` | `internal/agent/stream_stall.go`, … |
| `059d561a7` | `b66a2dba5` | `internal/agent/stream_stall.go`, … |

`b66a2dba5` was `HEAD` at the time. The three requested commits are unrelated to it and touch `internal/toolprocgate/`, `internal/gateway/`, and `internal/superloop/` respectively — none touches `internal/agent/`.

The argument is *declared*: passing it raises no validation error. It is accepted and dropped.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than documenting

The verdict is a **witness**. Its whole purpose is to answer "does commit X's diff do the kind of thing commit X's message claims". Auditing a different commit does not weaken that answer — it inverts it, because:

- The failure is **silent and directional**. A caller auditing an old, genuinely-unwitnessed commit gets `verdict: OK` whenever HEAD happens to be well-formed. The tool fails toward "witnessed", which is the unsafe direction for a gate.
- The response **self-reports a sha**, so a caller that logs the result records a true-looking statement about the wrong commit. Any downstream record built from this is mis-attributed at the source.
- Anything that closes issues on a commit-audit verdict is affected. The close-resolved arm's comments cite a resolving commit and say the close was "witnessed via `dos commit-audit` (verdict OK / diff-witnessed)". If the audit graded HEAD rather than the cited commit, the citation is not evidence for what it appears to attest.

Found while auditing a backlog of tickets that were fixed on trunk but never auto-closed, so the practical impact is not hypothetical — this is exactly the path that decides whether a fix is credited to its ticket.

## Note on the CLI

The installed `dos` CLI does not accept `--commit` at all (`dos: error: unrecognized arguments: --commit`), so the CLI and the MCP surface disagree about whether targeting a specific commit is even expressible. Worth settling both ways at once.

## Suggested resolution

Either honour `commit`, or reject it explicitly. A hard error on an argument that cannot be honoured is strictly better than a confident answer about the wrong object. If the audit is intentionally HEAD-only, the parameter should be removed from the schema and the tool should say so in its description.

Upstream note: the audit implementation lives in `dos-kernel`, so the fix likely belongs there; filing here because the close-resolved arm that consumes it operates on this repo's issues.

Records.Title: fix(gateway): a result-floor 502 on the streaming passthrough is never counted or printed, so the upstream-error metric silently under-reports
Records.Body:
## What

`internal/gateway/messages_stream_passthrough.go:449-450` is the one arm of the streaming
passthrough's terminal switch that returns **without counting or printing anything**:

```go
case p.wroteError:
    return true // a clean terminal HTTP error was already written
```

Its two siblings both observe and render. The mid-stream arm:

```go
s.renderTurnDebugError(reqTrace, "anthropic_messages", err, time.Since(began))
```

and the `default:` arm at :455-456:

```go
s.metrics.observeUpstreamError(err)
s.renderTurnDebugError(reqTrace, "anthropic_messages", err, time.Since(began))
```

So a turn that reaches the `p.wroteError` arm is invisible on `/metrics` and prints no `FAILED`
line on the default debug output. The comment is accurate about what happened — a clean terminal
HTTP error *was* written to the client — but "the client was told" and "the operator was told" are
different questions, and only the first is satisfied.

## Why it matters now

The reachable producer of `wroteError = true` is the **result-floor** branch at :241-248:

```go
adms, aerr := p.s.admitInboundResults(p.r.Context(), p.req.Messages, p.req.Tools, p.reqTrace)
if aerr != nil {
    p.s.logf("gateway: result-floor error (messages stream): %v", aerr)
    writeErr(p.w, http.StatusBadGateway, "upstream model error")
    p.wroteError = true
    return errPassthroughResponded
}
```

A result-floor rejection therefore returns a 502 to the caller and leaves **no operator-visible
trace except an `s.logf`**, which only reaches the `--log` stream — OFF by default. The
`default:` arm's own comment says exactly why that is not enough: "the `s.logf` calls below only
reach the --log stream, OFF by default". The same reasoning applies here and was not carried over.

The failure mode is the bad one: a class of 502s that never appears in the error metric, so the
`/metrics` upstream-error count under-reports and the gap is silent. Nobody notices a number that
is too small.

## Scope note

This was found while working #5491. That fix removes the *in-band refusal* caller from this arm —
before it, the pre-start in-band error path also set `wroteError` — so #5491 narrows what reaches
:449 but does **not** close this. The result-floor branch at :247 still takes it, which is why this
is filed separately rather than folded in.

## Suggested shape

Make the arm consistent with its siblings: `observeUpstreamError` + `renderTurnDebugError` before
returning, without re-writing to the client (the HTTP error is already sent — that part is
correct). Care is needed not to double-count if any future caller observes before setting the flag;
today's single producer at :247 does not, so a straight addition is currently exact.

A witness would assert that a result-floor rejection increments the upstream-error metric exactly
once and emits a debug line, while still writing exactly one 502 body.

## Confidence

**Verified by reading**, at the current tip: the three switch arms and their differing calls, that
:247 is the surviving producer of the flag, and that `writeErr` sends the body. Line numbers are
from the working tree with #5491's change applied — the arm itself is untouched by that change.

**Not reproduced:** I did not drive a live result-floor rejection and diff `/metrics` before and
after. That is the checkable next step and would confirm the under-count directly.

Records.Title: feat(modelroute): produce fak.modelroute.serving.v1 from a live gateway so the placement ladder's fleet rung stops being a hand-written file
Records.Body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`internal/modelroute` has a serving-liveness record and nothing in fak produces it.
`internal/modelroute/serving.go:76` declares:

```go
const ServingReportSchema = "fak.modelroute.serving.v1"
```

Grepping the whole tree for that string returns **only** `_test.go` fixtures
(`cmd/fak/route_place_serving_test.go`, eight occurrences) and one doc sample
(`docs/model-accounts.md:516`). The single ingestion point is `loadServingReport`
(`cmd/fak/route_place_serving.go:121-137`), which reads a path an operator passes with
`--serving <path>`.

So the **fleet rung of the placement ladder is gated by a hand-written JSON file.**
`modelroute.PlaceWithServing` walks device → fleet → vendor with a closed reason vocabulary
(`internal/modelroute/placement.go`, `zone.go`), and whether a fleet zone is admissible depends
entirely on a file a human remembered to refresh. Meanwhile a real prober sits one package away:
`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go` runs a health loop with hysteresis and drain and exposes
`Snapshot() []WorkerStatus` (`:261`). The two never meet — `Place`/`PlaceWithServing` has **zero
callers in `internal/gateway`** (only `cmd/fak/dispatch_rung_escalate.go:392`,
`cmd/fak/dispatch_rung_resolve.go:310`, `cmd/fak/route_place.go:172`).

`internal/modelroute/serving.go` is explicit that it does not intend to probe — *"Probing is
somebody else's job, above this tier."* This issue is that job.

## Why this is next

A placement decision that consults a stale operator file is worse than one that consults nothing:
it reports a **zone** verdict with the ladder's closed reason vocabulary, which reads as measured
when it is asserted. The producer is the smallest change that turns the ladder's fleet rung from a
convention into an observation, and every downstream multi-model decision (which zone, which
worker, which account) inherits its honesty.

## Working spine

A serve process that maintains a `FleetMembership` emits a `fak.modelroute.serving.v1` document
from its own `Snapshot()` — one entry per worker with its observed state and observation timestamp
— to a well-known path under the fleet state dir. `loadServingReport` gains a

Records.Title: feat(closeout): verify range-scoped secondary obligations from repository evidence
Records.Body:
## Parent context
#4636

## Summary

Add a repository closeout verifier that derives secondary obligations from a commit range and the current candidate paths instead of trusting an agent checklist.

fak already has specialized checks for documentation placement, generated indexes, release state, and witnessed completion. The missing layer is one bounded report that maps the actual change set to the follow-up artifacts it owes and returns repairable machine states.

## Scope

- Accept a commit range and, optionally, selected dirty paths.
- Drive obligation discovery from a declarative change-kind-to-artifact map.
- Emit one row per obligation with a closed state such as `paid`, `unpaid`, `unproven`, `no_candidates`, or `inherited`.
- Include candidate and checked counts so an empty range or empty selector cannot look clean.
- Render bounded repair missions without letting worker narration set the final verdict.
- Keep any lifecycle-hook adapter advisory and bounded; the verifier must be rerun after repairs.

## Done conditions

- Invalid or unreadable ranges return a typed could-not-run result.
- Generated-index, documentation, release, and tracker obligations can be registered without hard-coding them into the renderer.
- JSON and human output describe the same obligation rows and counts.
- A repair run cannot mark itself complete; only a fresh readback of the repository range can close the row.
- Synthetic fixtures cover paid, unpaid, inherited, empty-domain, and checker-unavailable cases.

## Proof requirement

Land a failing-first fixture where a primary change omits one declared secondary artifact, show the verifier naming the exact unpaid row, apply the repair, and independently rerun the verifier to a paid result. Include a second fixture proving an empty or invalid range cannot return an ordinary pass.

## Non-goals

This issue does not prescribe a release process or require every repository to enable the same obligation classes.

## Provenance

private workspace review

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/100 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- repositories: >= 1 tree

## Witnessed operating envelope
- repositories: 1 tree

Records.Title: test(policy): enforce implication contracts between layered validators
Records.Body:
## Parent context

Part of #4509.

## Problem

If one validator is described as a stricter form of another, every input accepted by the stricter validator must also satisfy the prerequisite validator. Testing each validator independently does not prove that relationship.

Fak has layered advisory, admission, verification, and blocking policies. Parallel implementations can accidentally let a “strict” path accept records rejected by its base trust gate.

## Proposed contract

Make this distinction explicit at the project boundary, preserve the inputs needed to audit it, and fail closed when the distinction cannot be established.

## Done when

1. - Declare prerequisite relationships between validator levels.
2. - Implement stricter validators by composing or reusing prerequisite validation.
3. - Add a relational property test: acceptance by a stricter level implies acceptance by every prerequisite.
4. - Exercise valid, absent, unstated, unknown, malformed, and internally inconsistent inputs.
5. - Include a planted inversion that passes both validators’ isolated tests but fails the implication test.
6. - Diagnostics identify the prerequisite layer that rejected the input.
7. - Test output states the evaluated domain size.

## Proof artifacts

- A committed machine-readable receipt demonstrates the accepted case and the refusal case.
- A committed known-positive fixture proves the signal can succeed.
- A committed adversarial or boundary fixture proves the contract cannot pass vacuously.
- Focused tests exercise the public result shape and every typed refusal used by the contract.

Identified through private workspace review.

Records.Title: feat(modelaccept): grade tool-call WIDTH per turn, not just MinToolCalls per task
Records.Body:
## Summary

`internal/modelaccept` can already require a **total** number of tool calls for a task
(`MinToolCalls`, `internal/modelaccept/modelaccept.go:28`, gated at `:162` and validated at
`:308`). It cannot express or grade **width** — how many of those calls the model issued in
a single turn. That makes the acceptance corpus blind to the one tool-use axis the
literature says separates models on long-horizon work, and it grades the axis that is
confounded with retries.

## The gap, concretely

`examples/model-acceptance-agentic-v1.json` has tasks like:

- `multi-step-tool` — "Use the provided read-only lookup tool at least twice", `min_tool_calls: 2`
- `retry-recovery` — "Call the provided flaky read-only tool ... retry once", `min_tool_calls: 2`

Both are satisfied identically by a model that issues two calls in two serialized turns and
by a model that issues two independent calls in one turn. Those are very different
capabilities. Worse, `retry-recovery` reaching `min_tool_calls: 2` is *by construction* a
retry — so the same field is being used to encode "the model batched" and "the model
failed once and recovered", which are opposite signals.

`examples/model-acceptance-prospective-v3-report.json` makes the conflation explicit — its
`production-multi-record` task asks for both records "in **separate** tool calls" while
still grading only the count.

## Why width belongs in acceptance

- [Wide & Deep](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07359v1) scales width (parallel calls per
  reasoning step) against depth and finds width raises accuracy *and* lowers turn count —
  62.2% with GPT-5-Medium on BrowseComp vs the 54.9% originally reported for GPT-5-High.
  Width is a capability, and it is the capability that pays.
- Provider support is genuinely uneven, so it is a real acceptance question rather than a
  formality: some model families reject `parallel_tool_calls` outright while their
  successors support it, meaning "can this model batch at all" is a routing-relevant fact
  fak should know before it pins a model to a lane.
- Volume alone misleads. A 1,440-run MCP benchmark found retry rate inflating cost 1.4-2.8x;
  models at 75% first-attempt pass reach 96-98% only with up to 3 retries. A corpus that
  rewards call count rewards the failing model.

## Proposal

Add a width axis to the task schema and the fold, kept strictly separate from the existing
volume field:

- `min_parallel_tool_calls` (or a `max_tool_turns` sibling) — a task can require that N
  independent calls arrive in ONE assistant turn, not merely N calls overall.
- Record per-run `tool_turns` alongside the existing `ToolCalls`, so the fold can derive
  calls-per-turn using the **same denominator convention** as
  `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` rather than inventing a third definition of the same ratio.
- Report width per model in the acceptance report as a first-class dimension, so
  "better models batch more" becomes a graded, reproducible claim about *this* corpus
  instead of an inherited assumption.
- Add at least one genuinely parallel-friendly task: two independent lookups with **no**
  data dependency, where a one-turn solution is strictly better and the corpus can tell.

Keep `MinToolCalls` as-is for the retry/recovery tasks where total count is the right
question. The point is to stop one field carrying two meanings.

## Acceptance criteria

- A task can declare a per-turn width requirement, validated the way `MinToolCalls` is
  (`:308` rejects a width requirement without `tool_required`).
- The report carries a per-model width figure using `turnbatch`'s denominator convention.
- A corpus task exists whose independent-calls-in-one-turn solution is distinguishable from
  the serialized solution, and the fold distinguishes them (table test with both run shapes).
- Existing corpora keep their current verdicts (the new field is additive and optional).

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Shares the width definition with the orphan-KPI child —
those two should agree on the denominator, or the fleet meter and the acceptance grade will
disagree about the same model.

  reasoning step) against depth and finds width raises accuracy *and* lowers turn count —
  62.2% with GPT-5-Medium on BrowseComp vs the 54.9% originally reported for GPT-5-High.
  Width is a capability, and it is the capability that pays.
- Provider support is genuinely uneven, so it is a real acceptance question rather than a
  formality: some model families reject `parallel_tool_calls` outright while their
  successors support it, meaning "can this model batch at all" is a routing-relevant fact
  fak should know before it pins a model to a lane.
- Volume alone misleads. A 1,440-run MCP benchmark found retry rate inflating cost 1.4-2.8x;
  models at 75% first-attempt pass reach 96-98% only with up to 3 retries. A corpus that
  rewards call count rewards the failing model.

## Proposal

Add a width axis to the task schema and the fold, kept strictly separate from the existing
volume field:

- `min_parallel_tool_calls` (or a `max_tool_turns` sibling) — a task can require that N
  independent calls arrive in ONE assistant turn, not merely N calls overall.
- Record per-run `tool_turns` alongside the existing `ToolCalls`, so the fold can derive
  calls-per-turn using the **same denominator convention** as
  `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` rather than inventing a third definition of the same ratio.
- Report width per model in the acceptance report as a first-class dimension, so
  "better models batch more" becomes a graded, reproducible claim about *this* corpus
  instead of an inherited assumption.
- Add at least one genuinely parallel-friendly task: two independent lookups with **no**
  data dependency, where a one-turn solution is strictly better and the corpus can tell.

Keep `MinToolCalls` as-is for the retry/recovery tasks where total count is the right
question. The point is to stop one field carrying two meanings.

- A task can declare a per-turn width requirement, validated the way `MinToolCalls` is
  (`:308` rejects a width requirement without `tool_required`).
- The report carries a per-model width figure using `turnbatch`'s denominator convention.
- A corpus task exists whose independent-calls-in-one-turn solution is distinguishable from
  the serialized solution, and the fold distinguishes them (table test with both run shapes).
- Existing corpora keep their current verdicts (the new field is additive and optional).

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Shares the width definition with the orphan-KPI child —
those two should agree on the denominator, or the fleet meter and the acceptance grade will
disagree about the same model.

Records.Title: A dead worker's lane lease blocks its lane forever: acquire never applies the kernel's own dead-lease filter, and no reap verb is exposed
Records.Body:
## Symptom

The `tools` lane was held by worker `w4591` from **2026-07-18** until tonight (**2026-08-06**) — 19 days. Every peer that asked for the lane was refused:

```
$ dos lease-lane acquire --lane tools --owner <peer>
reason = lane 'tools' is already held by a live loop - pick a different --lane or wait.
```

Lane-journal seq 2294 shows the same refusal issued to an unrelated peer (`harvest-recovery`), so this was chronic, not a race. `w4591` had been dead the whole time.

## The holder was provably dead, and the kernel can already prove it

```
$ python -c "from dos import proc_delta; print(proc_delta.probe(80596, host_id='DESKTOP-BB3FMHP', this_host='DESKTOP-BB3FMHP', recorded_starttime=134288779379632999))"
ProcLiveness(alive=False, detail='pid 80596 is gone (win32 INVALID_PARAMETER)')
```

Same host, so the local pid+`proc_starttime` probe is authoritative (no cross-host TTL overlay needed). Both arms of the kernel's own `_lease_is_dead` predicate (`lane_lease.py:224`) were satisfied: heartbeat-stale far past TTL **and** confirmed-dead holder pid.

## Root cause

`lane_lease.live_leases(config, *, expire_dead: bool = False)` — the dead-lease filter is **opt-in and defaults OFF**. `acquire()` (`lane_lease.py:389`) deliberately passes the structural fold:

```python
live = live_leases(config) + extra   # expire_dead=False, by design
```

The in-code rationale is sound for its own case: `expire_dead=True` would probe the pid of a *fresh* lease whose short-lived journaling subprocess has already exited, report `alive=False`, and let a racing acquirer double-book (the TOCTOU the lease exists to prevent; it previously regressed `test_coord_demo_k4_serializes_writes`).

But the consequence is that **the authority path never self-heals**. A lease whose holder died has no expiry on the only call that grants lanes. Only two callers pass `expire_dead=True` (`cli.py:6330`, `cli.py:8377`) and neither grants a lane.

## No reap verb is exposed

`dos lease-lane` offers exactly `{acquire, release, heartbeat, spawn, live}`. The two functions that *are* meant to clear an orphan have **no CLI surface at all**:

- `lane_lease.adopt()` (`lane_lease.py:559`) — no `add_parser("adopt")`, no caller in `cli.py`.
- `SCAVENGE` — recognised as a journal op (`cli.py:8590` `_QUEUE_DRAIN_OPS`) but nothing emits it from the CLI.

`live_leases`' own docstring says the dead orphan is kept visible "precisely so [`adopt()` and the orphan-reclaim sweep] can transfer/scavenge it" — but neither is reachable by an operator.

## The workaround I used (undocumented, and too blunt)

`release()` matches on `holder == owner`, so naming the dead holder works:

```
$ dos lease-lane release --lane tools --owner w4591
{"lane": "tools", "owner": "w4591", "released": true}
```

This is append-only and auditable, but it is indistinguishable from a legitimate self-release: it asserts no liveness check, so it will just as happily evict a **live** holder. It is a footgun, not a reap.

## Why this is worth fixing

This is the same defect class as the goal-park bug fixed tonight: **state that outlives the condition that created it, with no sanctioned way to clear it.** A single crashed worker permanently removes a lane from the fleet, and the blast radius grows monotonically — `dos lease-lane live` currently shows leases still held from 2026-07-16 by `fable-superloop-23874`, `ultracode-5025`, `goal-4876`, and others, all with the same shape.

## Suggested fix

Expose a reap verb that applies the liveness predicate the kernel already has, rather than trusting the caller:

```
dos lease-lane reap --lane <name> [--owner <holder>]
```

refusing unless `_lease_is_dead(lease, now, this_host)` holds, and journaling a `SCAVENGE` (already in `_QUEUE_DRAIN_OPS`). That keeps `acquire()`'s TOCTOU-safe structural fold untouched — the self-heal becomes an explicit, evidence-gated operator action instead of an implicit read-time elision.

Records.Title: region admission: a sub-lane passed to --lane resolves to no tree and collides with everything (regionadmit never adopted laneadmit's hierarchy)
Records.Body:
## Summary

`internal/laneadmit` now understands hierarchical lane names (`gateway/server`,
`gateway/server.go`), landed in d41f5605a8. `internal/regionadmit` — the *other* pure
admission twin, and the one every real surface actually calls — does not. The two twins
have diverged, and on the surface a user touches the divergence is not neutral: passing a
sub-lane to `--lane` today is **strictly worse** than passing its declared root.

## Reproduced from the code

`fak loop region` (`cmd/fak/loop_region.go:83,93-94`), `fak loop drive`, and the dispatch
tick all go through `regionadmit.Decide` / `regionadmit.ResolveTree`.

**1. A sub-lane resolves to NO tree, so it collides with everything.**

`regionadmit.ResolveTree` (`internal/regionadmit/regionadmit.go:94-102`) resolves a lane by
exact map lookup:

```go
if req.Lane != "" {
    return cleanGlobs(tax.Trees[req.Lane])   // :99
}
```

`tax.Trees` is keyed by declared lane name only, so `--lane gateway/server` misses and
returns `nil`. Rung 4 (`:287`, `dispatchorder.TreesOverlap`) reads an empty tree as unknown
blast radius and collides **conservatively against every live lease**. So the narrower name
a worker types to get *more* concurrency gets it *less*: `--lane gateway` is admitted
against a disjoint peer, `--lane gateway/server` is refused by any peer at all.

`laneadmit.Taxonomy.TreeFor` (`internal/laneadmit/lanetree.go:193`) is the fixed version —
it walks to the nearest declared ancestor and derives `internal/gateway/server/**`.

**2. Exclusivity does not inherit downward.**

Rung 1 (`internal/regionadmit/regionadmit.go:251`) is a direct lookup:

```go
if tax.Exclusive[req.Lane] && len(others) > 0 {
```

`tax.Exclusive["abi/registry.go"]` is false, so a sub-lane of an exclusive root does not
trip the runs-alone gate at rung 1. In practice defect 1 masks this (the empty tree refuses
at rung 4 anyway, and with nothing live an exclusive request admits regardless), so this is
a latent hole rather than a live escape — but it becomes a real one the moment defect 1 is
fixed without fixing this. `laneadmit.Taxonomy.IsExclusive`
(`internal/laneadmit/lanetree.go:169`) walks ancestors for exactly this reason.

**3. Same-lane comparison is string equality.**

`:268` `if req.Lane != "" && lane == req.Lane` never fires for a parent/child pair, so
`gateway` and `gateway/server` would not serialize against each other even though the
parent may edit anywhere beneath the child. `laneadmit` reports this as its own rung,
`ConflictLaneAncestry` (`internal/laneadmit/laneadmit.go:36,158`).

Note the two twins also carry **different `Taxonomy` types** — `regionadmit.Taxonomy` has no
`Loaded` field and its own `LoadTaxonomy` (`:317`), so this is not a one-line import.

## What would fix it

Either port the four helpers (`CanonicalLane`, `LaneContains`, `TreeFor`, `IsExclusive`) into
`regionadmit`, or — better, and the reason the algebra was kept pure and dependency-light —
have `regionadmit` build a `laneadmit.Taxonomy` and delegate the lane-name dimension to it,
leaving `regionadmit`'s narrowed-pair co-admit rung (`strictlyWithinLane`, `:149`) as the
geometry half. Prefer the second: two independent implementations of one contract is how
this drifted in the first place.

This changes the **live** admission path that `fak dispatch tick` and `fak loop drive`
already run, so it wants its own change, not a drive-by.

## Acceptance bar

- `--lane gateway/server` resolves to `internal/gateway/server/**`, not `nil`.
- `--lane abi/registry.go` trips `exclusive_lane_requested`.
- `gateway` vs `gateway/server` serialize; `gateway/server` vs `gateway/router` co-run.
- Every existing `internal/regionadmit` test passes unchanged — all 543 declared lanes are a
  single `[a-z0-9]+` segment, so flat verdicts must stay byte-identical (this is the property
  `laneadmit`'s `TestDecideFlatVerdictsUnchanged` pins on its side).

## Not this issue

This does **not** by itself raise fleet concurrency. No surface picks a sub-lane on its own —
`fak dispatch wave` still routes an issue to a declared leaf — and #5854 is the blocker for
that (the lease record conflates admission geometry with authorization geometry, so narrowing
only the pricer yields phantom concurrency). This issue is the prerequisite: the decision has
to understand a sub-lane before anything can usefully hand it one.

Docs state the gap today: `docs/region-admission.md` (`Sub-lanes` + `Honest boundary`).
